title: Queue Storage, Table Storage, and Disk Storage
description: Explore Azure Queue Storage for messaging, Table Storage for NoSQL data, and managed disks for virtual machines.

data.text: Beyond Blob Storage and Files, Azure offers additional storage services for specific workloads: Queue Storage for messaging between apps, Table Storage for simple NoSQL data, and managed disks for virtual machines.

Queue Storage is a service for storing large numbers of messages. A single queue can contain millions of messages, and each message can be up to 64 KB. It's used to decouple application components so they can scale independently.

Table Storage is a NoSQL key-value store for semi-structured data. It's simple, fast, and very cost-effective for scenarios like storing user profiles, device information, or metadata. It is not a replacement for a full relational database.

Managed Disks are persistent disks for Azure Virtual Machines. Azure handles the storage account management, and you just choose the disk type and size. Managed disks come in several types optimized for different performance and cost needs.

data.title: When Not to Use Table Storage
data.text: Table Storage is not a relational database. If you need complex queries, joins, or transactions, use Azure SQL Database or Cosmos DB instead.

data.title: Create a Queue and Add a Message with Azure CLI
data.content: Use the Azure CLI extension for storage to work with queues.
data.code:
# Install the storage extension if needed
az extension add --name storage-preview

# Create a storage account
az storage account create \
  --name mystorageaccount123 \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

# Create a queue
az storage queue create \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --name myqueue

# Add a message to the queue
az storage message put \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --queue-name myqueue \
  --content 'Hello from Azure Queue Storage!'

# Peek at the next message (without removing it)
az storage message peek \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --queue-name myqueue

# Get and delete the message
az storage message get \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --queue-name myqueue

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Queue Storage is for messaging between application components
Table Storage is a simple, fast NoSQL key-value store
Managed Disks provide persistent storage for Azure VMs
Each storage type is optimized for a specific workload
data.takeaway: Azure gives you a dedicated storage service for almost every scenario. Pick the one that matches your workload rather than forcing everything into Blob Storage.
